A '''WED-15 Treadwell''' [[Maintenance droid/Legends|repair droid]], produced by the [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]] company, worked for [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A [[Class five droid/Legends|fifth-degree]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]], the Treadwell sometimes misidentified the noise of [[Sandfly/Legends|sand flies]] for malfunctioning equipment and followed them.

==Biography==
A [[WED-15 Treadwell droid/Legends|WED-15 Treadwell]] [[Maintenance droid/Legends|repair droid]] was produced by<ref name="DB" /> [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]], one of the two largest [[Droid/Legends|droid]]-manufacturing companies in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="TEGTTD" /> prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="ANH" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the droid became one of several [[WED Treadwell repair droid/Legends|Treadwells]] working for [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars's]] [[Lars family/Legends|family]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], alongside the droid [[WED-15-77/Legends|WED-15-77]], which served on the [[Lars homestead/Legends|farm]] for more than twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]].<ref name="DB" />

==Characteristics==
As a [[Class five droid/Legends|fifth-degree]] droid,<ref name="TEGTTD" /> the Treadwell had only limited intelligence. Sometimes, it followed [[Sandfly/Legends|sand flies]], misidentifying their noise as that of a malfunctioning piece of equipment.<ref name="locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> [[Color/Legends|Colored]] blue, the droid was a typical Treadwell repair unit, possessing two rows of ten treaded [[wheel]]s on its base. The droid's binocular [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] were black and were mounted on a long, telescopic stalk, which also held its manipulator [[Limb/Legends|arms]].<ref name="DB" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Treadwell-bts.jpg|thumb|left|150px|John Barry's production sketch of a Treadwell droid]]
The model used for the as-yet unnamed WED-15 Treadwell was designed in [[1975]] by production designer [[John Barry]] for use in the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="making">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> The same droid model was also used for the droids [[WED-15-I662]] and [[WED-15-77/Legends|WED-15-77]] during the filming of the movie.<ref name="DB" /> Barry's notes showed that the prop had one functioning arm and housed a radio controller in its treadwell base so that it could be controlled by off-screen crew members. Barry's sketch indicated that the model stood between four feet and four feet, six inches tall. Scenes featuring the droid were shot on location in [[Tunisia]] in [[March]] [[1976]].<ref name="making" />

The Treadwell droid first appeared in ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'', written and directed by [[George Lucas]] and released on [[May 25]], [[1977]]. [[Dorling Kindersley]]'s ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'' incorrectly identified this droid as "[[WED 15 Septoid 2]],"<ref name="locations" /> which is another type of Treadwell droid.<ref name="VD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

The meltdown scene of WED-15-77, a similarly-appearing Treadwell, occurred before the appearance of the unidentified Treadwell in the film.<ref name="DB" /> In the film's [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama]], however, WED-15-77 merely stopped moving rather than melting down, and Owen Lars mentioned at a later [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] auction that he had "already got a Treadwell [and didn't] need [[WED-15-ST68/Legends|another]]." This suggested that the unidentified droid was intended to be WED-15-77<ref name="radio drama">[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]], ep. 4</ref> and not another droid of the same line. However, the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] confirmed WED-15-77's meltdown to be final and the droids to be separate characters.<ref name="DB" />
